cr_title: Edaphic controls on genome size and GC content of bacteria in soil microbial communities
relevance: Demonstrates that high-pH and carbon-limited soils select for smaller genomes with higher GC content, supporting our observation that group 1l carriers exhibit elevated GC without genome expansion.
title: Edaphic controls on genome size and GC content of bacteria in soil microbial communities

cr_title: Codon bias, nucleotide selection, and genome size predict in situ bacterial growth rate and transcription in rewetted soil
cr_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Validates via 18O-water stable isotope probing that ribosomal codon usage bias directly predicts in situ bacterial growth rates in soil, validating our gRodon-predicted doubling time estimates.
title: Codon bias, nucleotide selection, and genome size predict in situ bacterial growth rate and transcription in rewetted soil

cr_title: Elevational Constraints on the Composition and Genomic Attributes of Microbial Communities in Antarctic Soils
relevance: Shows across an extreme arid Antarctic gradient that severe environmental stress selects for lower predicted maximum growth rates and an overrepresentation of trace-gas scavenging genes.
title: Elevational Constraints on the Composition and Genomic Attributes of Microbial Communities in Antarctic Soils

cr_title: Warmer and drier ecosystems select for smaller bacterial genomes in global soils
relevance: Finds across 237 global soil sites that aridity selects for smaller bacterial genomes, challenging our finding that Rub' al-Khali group 1h, 2a, and form-I CoxL carriers possess larger genomes.
title: Warmer and drier ecosystems select for smaller bacterial genomes in global soils

cr_title: Environmental stress leads to genome streamlining in a widely distributed species of soil bacteria
relevance: Shows that environmental stressors including aridity drive continuous genome reduction in soil bacteria, contrasting with our observation that non-1l trace-gas scavengers maintain expanded genomes.
title: Environmental stress leads to genome streamlining in a widely distributed species of soil bacteria

cr_title: Atmospheric hydrogen consumption is regulated by glycerol-mediated catabolite repression in mycobacteria
relevance: Demonstrates that consumption of atmospheric H2 via group 1l [NiFe]-hydrogenase (Huc) is repressed by labile organic carbon through catabolite repression, explaining group 1l depletion beside plant roots.
title: Atmospheric hydrogen consumption is regulated by glycerol-mediated catabolite repression in mycobacteria

cr_title: Aridity drives global convergence of desert microbiomes and biogeochemical activities
relevance: Demonstrates across global desert MAGs that aridity drives convergent genome reduction to ~3.7 Mb and widespread dependence on atmospheric chemosynthesis.
title: Aridity drives global convergence of desert microbiomes and biogeochemical activities

cr_title: Acidobacteria are active and abundant members of diverse atmospheric H2-oxidizing communities detected in temperate soils
relevance: Establishes that group 1h [NiFe]-hydrogenases are prevalent across oligotrophic soil bacteria and mediate persistence under carbon starvation, contextualizing group 1h carriers as slow-growing persistence specialists.
title: Acidobacteria are active and abundant members of diverse atmospheric H2-oxidizing communities detected in temperate soils

cr_title: Metabolic versatility of soil microbial communities below the rocks of the hyperarid Dalangtan Playa
relevance: Identifies widespread form I CoxL and group 1 [NiFe]-hydrogenases across hyperarid desert soils, demonstrating the ecological importance of CO and H2 scavenging in hyperarid environments.
title: Metabolic versatility of soil microbial communities below the rocks of the hyperarid Dalangtan Playa

cr_title: Atmospheric Trace Gas Oxidizers Contribute to Soil Carbon Fixation Driven by Key Soil Conditions in Terrestrial Ecosystems
relevance: Finds that the abundances of hyd and coxL genes peak in desert soils and decrease with soil moisture, supporting our finding that trace-gas scavengers are depleted in moister root-adjacent microhabitats.
title: Atmospheric Trace Gas Oxidizers Contribute to Soil Carbon Fixation Driven by Key Soil Conditions in Terrestrial Ecosystems

cr_title: Exploiting rRNA operon copy number to investigate bacterial reproductive strategies
relevance: Connects low translational machinery investment with slow maximum growth rates and resource-conserving oligotrophic lifestyles, supporting our interpretation of longer predicted doubling times in trace-gas carriers.
title: Exploiting rRNA operon copy number to investigate bacterial reproductive strategies

cr_title: Genome reduction in an abundant and ubiquitous soil bacterium ‘Candidatus Udaeobacter copiosus’
relevance: Characterizes the genomic archetype of soil oligotrophic streamlining, providing a benchmark to contrast against the expanded genomes of metabolically versatile trace-gas oxidizers.
title: Genome reduction in an abundant and ubiquitous soil bacterium 'Candidatus Udaeobacter copiosus'

cr_title: Microbial oxidation of atmospheric trace gases
relevance: Reviews the physiological distinctions between scavenging hydrogenases (groups 1h, 1l) and mixotrophic enzymes (group 2a, form I CoxL), clarifying why genomic carriers show divergent genome size adaptations.
title: Microbial oxidation of atmospheric trace gases

cr_title: Significant Impacts of Increasing Aridity on the Arid Soil Microbiome
relevance: Shows that hyperaridity drastically constrains active biomass while selecting for desiccation-tolerant taxa, emphasizing that read-based marker abundances quantify genomic capacity rather than instantaneous metabolic activity.
title: Significant Impacts of Increasing Aridity on the Arid Soil Microbiome

cr_title: Carbon amendments in soil microcosms induce uneven response on H2 oxidation activity and microbial community composition
relevance: Demonstrates that labile organic carbon amendments (sucrose) induce catabolic repression of soil atmospheric H2 oxidation and deplete high-affinity hydrogenase genes (hhyL), directly mirroring the depletion of scavengers beside plant roots.
title: Carbon amendments in soil microcosms induce uneven response on H2 oxidation activity and microbial community composition

cr_title: Persistence of the dominant soil phylum Acidobacteria by trace gas scavenging
cr_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Proves in the soil isolate Pyrinomonas methylaliphatogenes that high-affinity [NiFe]-hydrogenase is specifically upregulated upon carbon exhaustion to support starvation survival rather than mixotrophic growth on glucose.
title: Persistence of the dominant soil phylum Acidobacteria by trace gas scavenging

cr_title: Breathing air to save energy – new insights into the ecophysiological role of high‐affinity [NiFe]‐hydrogenase in Streptomyces avermitilis
relevance: Shows that high-affinity group 1h [NiFe]-hydrogenase expression in Streptomyces avermitilis is localized to spores to scavenge atmospheric H2 and conserve endogenous energy reserves during carbon starvation.
title: Breathing air to save energy – new insights into the ecophysiological role of high-affinity [NiFe]-hydrogenase in Streptomyces avermitilis

cr_title: Two uptake hydrogenases differentially interact with the aerobic respiratory chain during mycobacterial growth and persistence
relevance: Demonstrates distinct physiological functions where group 2a (Huc) operates during late exponential growth while group 1h (Hhy) supports long-term persistence upon organic carbon exhaustion.
title: Two uptake hydrogenases differentially interact with the aerobic respiratory chain during mycobacterial growth and persistence

cr_title: Genomic evidence for aerotrophy as a defining trait of Ktedonobacteria inhabiting silica-rich oligotrophic caves
relevance: Demonstrates that aerotrophy mediated by group 1h/1l [NiFe]-hydrogenases and Form I CoxL is a core genomic adaptation of Chloroflexota to severely carbon-starved, oligotrophic subterranean environments.
title: Genomic evidence for aerotrophy as a defining trait of Ktedonobacteria inhabiting silica-rich oligotrophic caves

cr_title: Widespread horizontal transfer and strong selection enhance microbial adaptation in Antarctic soils
relevance: Documents that group 1l [NiFe]-hydrogenase (HylLS) genes undergo widespread horizontal gene transfer and purifying selection across phyla to sustain survival in hyperarid, carbon-starved mineral soils.
title: Widespread horizontal transfer and strong selection enhance microbial adaptation in Antarctic soils

cr_title: Simultaneous Oxidation of Atmospheric Methane, Carbon Monoxide and Hydrogen for Bacterial Growth
relevance: Proves that bacteria can simultaneously co-oxidize atmospheric trace gases (H2, CO, CH4) to actively support cellular growth, challenging the premise that high-affinity trace gas scavenging is restricted to starvation survival.
title: Simultaneous Oxidation of Atmospheric Methane, Carbon Monoxide and Hydrogen for Bacterial Growth

cr_title: Molecular Hydrogen, a Neglected Key Driver of Soil Biogeochemical Processes
relevance: Synthesizes evidence for survival mixotrophy, outlining how atmospheric H2 scavenging maintains dormant microbial seedbanks during organic carbon starvation in bulk soil.
title: Molecular Hydrogen, a Neglected Key Driver of Soil Biogeochemical Processes

cr_title: Distribution of Mixotrophy and Desiccation Survival Mechanisms across Microbial Genomes in an Arid Biological Soil Crust Community
relevance: Reveals widespread genomic capacity for mixotrophic trace gas scavenging and desiccation tolerance in desert biocrusts, challenging a simple binary division between heterotrophic growth and lithotrophic starvation survival.
title: Distribution of Mixotrophy and Desiccation Survival Mechanisms across Microbial Genomes in an Arid Biological Soil Crust Community

cr_title: Three different [ NiFe ] hydrogenases confer metabolic flexibility in the obligate aerobe M ycobacterium smegmatis
relevance: Demonstrates that group 1h (Hhy) hydrogenase is specifically upregulated upon organic carbon exhaustion, confirming that high-affinity scavenging is an inducible starvation-survival response.
title: Three different [NiFe] hydrogenases confer metabolic flexibility in the obligate aerobe Mycobacterium smegmatis

cr_title: Average genome size estimation improves comparative metagenomics and sheds light on the functional ecology of the human microbiome
relevance: Introduces MicrobeCensus to estimate average genome size and genome equivalents from universal single-copy genes, enabling per-cell normalisation of functional gene abundance.
title: Average genome size estimation improves comparative metagenomics and sheds light on the functional ecology of the human microbiome

cr_title: MUSiCC: a marker genes based framework for metagenomic normalization and accurate profiling of gene abundances in the microbiome
relevance: Demonstrates that universal single-copy marker gene coverage normalisation corrects for genome-size variation and sequencing depth disparities to yield accurate average genomic copy numbers.
title: MUSiCC: a marker genes based framework for metagenomic normalization and accurate profiling of gene abundances in the microbiome

cr_title: ROCker: accurate detection and quantification of target genes in short-read metagenomic data sets by modeling sliding-window bitscores
relevance: Demonstrates that uniform E-value or bitscore cutoffs generate high rates of false positives across homologous enzymes, justifying position-specific or competitive threshold modeling for read-based target gene quantification.
title: ROCker: accurate detection and quantification of target genes in short-read metagenomic data sets by modeling sliding-window bitscores

cr_title: Comparative Analysis of Functional Metagenomic Annotation and the Mappability of Short Reads
relevance: Quantifies short-read mis-annotation across homologous gene families and phylogenetic divergence, demonstrating that read-based homology searches can produce false positive functional assignments.
title: Comparative Analysis of Functional Metagenomic Annotation and the Mappability of Short Reads

cr_title: Assessing the performance of different approaches for functional and taxonomic annotation of metagenomes
relevance: Benchmarks synthetic metagenomes to show that direct translated read mapping suffers from substantial over-prediction and false positives in homologous functional gene families relative to contig-based annotation.
title: Assessing the performance of different approaches for functional and taxonomic annotation of metagenomes

cr_title: GC bias affects genomic and metagenomic reconstructions, underrepresenting GC-poor organisms
relevance: Demonstrates that Illumina shotgun sequencing incurs marked GC-dependent coverage distortions, raising the caveat that higher GC content in group 1l carrier genomes could systematically influence their read-based detection.
title: GC bias affects genomic and metagenomic reconstructions, underrepresenting GC-poor organisms

cr_title: LEMMI: a continuous benchmarking platform for metagenomics classifiers
relevance: Uses blind benchmarks on simulated communities to show how sequence divergence, unrepresented environmental taxa, and genome size differences introduce errors into short-read classifier abundance estimates.
title: LEMMI: a continuous benchmarking platform for metagenomics classifiers

cr_title: Sensitive protein alignments at tree-of-life scale using DIAMOND
relevance: Evaluates DIAMOND alignment sensitivity modes, confirming that translated search against comprehensive protein databases recovers true homologous alignments with high specificity at massive metagenomic read scale.
title: Sensitive protein alignments at tree-of-life scale using DIAMOND

cr_title: Integrating taxonomic, functional, and strain-level profiling of diverse microbial communities with bioBakery 3
relevance: Benchmarks translated DIAMOND search against comprehensive protein databases in mock communities, validating read-based functional gene profiling across uncharacterized environmental genomes.
title: Integrating taxonomic, functional, and strain-level profiling of diverse microbial communities with bioBakery 3

cr_title: Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation: the second round of challenges
relevance: Provides an independent community benchmark across complex multi-strain mock metagenomes, evaluating how database composition and read mapping cutoffs impact precision in environmental datasets.
title: Critical Assessment of Metagenome Interpretation: the second round of challenges

cr_title: METABOLIC: high-throughput profiling of microbial genomes for functional traits, metabolism, biogeochemistry, and community-scale functional networks
relevance: Defines profile-HMM and motif criteria for hydrogenases and trace-gas oxidizers, validating the mapping of genomic capacity to biogeochemical traits across complex environmental communities.
title: METABOLIC: high-throughput profiling of microbial genomes for functional traits, metabolism, biogeochemistry, and community-scale functional networks

cr_title: CoverM: read alignment statistics for metagenomics
relevance: Implements robust coverage statistics and genome-equivalent calculations from BAM alignments, providing reproducible standards to avoid coverage outlier artifacts in read-based gene quantification.
title: CoverM: read alignment statistics for metagenomics

cr_title: Comprehensive taxonomic identification of microbial species in metagenomic data using SingleM and Sandpiper
relevance: Demonstrates that direct short-read alignment to universal single-copy ribosomal protein marker genes provides accurate taxon abundance and genome-equivalent baselines without reference-genome dependence.
title: Comprehensive taxonomic identification of microbial species in metagenomic data using SingleM and Sandpiper

cr_title: GCompip: a pipeline for estimating the gene abundance in microbial communities
relevance: Validates universal single-copy gene normalization on mock communities across diverse biomes, demonstrating that per-cell normalisation prevents false gene abundance inflation observed in uncorrected metrics.
title: GCompip: a pipeline for estimating the gene abundance in microbial communities

cr_title: Diversity and geographical distribution of potential carbon monoxide oxidizers using molybdenum-containing enzymes in the ocean
relevance: Refines diagnostic active-site motif definitions for Form I CoxL (e.g. AYACSFR, AYRCSFR, SYRCSFR) to prevent overestimation of aerobic CO-oxidizing potential in metagenomic datasets.
title: Diversity and geographical distribution of potential carbon monoxide oxidizers using molybdenum-containing enzymes in the ocean

cr_title: Reconstructing Genomes of Carbon Monoxide Oxidisers in Volcanic Deposits Including Members of the Class Ktedonobacteria
relevance: Validates that distinguishing Form I (AYRCSFR) from Form II (AYRGAGR) in metagenome-assembled genomes reliably identifies bacteria capable of trace CO scavenging in arid, oligotrophic soils.
title: Reconstructing Genomes of Carbon Monoxide Oxidisers in Volcanic Deposits Including Members of the Class Ktedonobacteria

cr_title: Hydrogen and Carbon Monoxide-Utilizing Kyrpidia spormannii Species From Pantelleria Island, Italy
relevance: Demonstrates that Kyrpidia spormannii strains harboring exclusively Form II CoxL with the AYRGAGR motif can grow autotrophically via aerobic CO oxidation, challenging the assumption that Form II cannot oxidize CO.
title: Hydrogen and Carbon Monoxide-Utilizing Kyrpidia spormannii Species From Pantelleria Island, Italy

cr_title: Halobacterium bonnevillei sp. nov., Halobaculum saliterrae sp. nov. and Halovenus carboxidivorans sp. nov., three novel carbon monoxide-oxidizing Halobacteria from saline crusts and soils
cr_journal: International Journal of Systematic and Evolutionary Microbiology
relevance: Confirms that novel haloarchaea from hyperarid salt crusts encode canonical Form I coxL and functionally oxidize atmospheric CO, demonstrating that Form I typing captures trace gas scavengers in arid crustal soils.
title: Halobacterium bonnevillei sp. nov., Halobaculum saliterrae sp. nov. and Halovenus carboxidivorans sp. nov., three novel carbon monoxide-oxidizing Halobacteria from saline crusts and soils

cr_title: Identification of Unknown Carboxydovore Bacteria Dominant in Deciduous Forest Soil via Succession of Bacterial Communities, coxL Genotypes, and Carbon Monoxide Oxidation Activity in Soil Microcosms
relevance: Correlates high-affinity atmospheric CO uptake directly with the relative abundance of Form I coxL genotypes (AYXCSFR) across soil microcosms, supporting the focus on Form I as the functional sink.
title: Identification of Unknown Carboxydovore Bacteria Dominant in Deciduous Forest Soil via Succession of Bacterial Communities, coxL Genotypes, and Carbon Monoxide Oxidation Activity in Soil Microcosms

cr_title: Land-use influences the distribution and activity of high affinity CO-oxidizing bacteria associated to type I-coxL genotype in soil
relevance: Demonstrates that high-affinity atmospheric CO oxidation in soils is driven specifically by type I coxL abundance and diversity rather than type II genotypes.
title: Land-use influences the distribution and activity of high affinity CO-oxidizing bacteria associated to type I-coxL genotype in soil

cr_title: Correlating carbon monoxide oxidation with cox genes in the abundant Marine Roseobacter Clade
relevance: Demonstrates experimentally that bacterial isolates with only Form II coxL fail to consume CO, whereas only isolates possessing Form I coxL show active CO oxidation.
title: Correlating carbon monoxide oxidation with cox genes in the abundant Marine Roseobacter Clade

cr_title: Distribution and diversity of carbon monoxide‐oxidizing bacteria and bulk bacterial communities across a succession gradient on a Hawaiian volcanic deposit
relevance: Establishes primer sets and phylogenetic discriminators separating Form I (AYXCSFR) and Form II (AYRGAGR) coxL, demonstrating their distinct ecological distribution across soil gradients.
title: Distribution and diversity of carbon monoxide-oxidizing bacteria and bulk bacterial communities across a succession gradient on a Hawaiian volcanic deposit

cr_title: Purification and characterization of carbon monoxide dehydrogenase from the aerobic hyperthermophilic archaeon Aeropyrum pernix
relevance: Purified active aerobic CODH from the archaeon Aeropyrum pernix that lacks the canonical Form I cysteine motif, indicating that non-Form I active-site configurations can mediate aerobic CO oxidation.
title: Purification and characterization of carbon monoxide dehydrogenase from the aerobic hyperthermophilic archaeon Aeropyrum pernix

cr_title: The CoxD Protein of Oligotropha carboxidovorans Is a Predicted AAA+ ATPase Chaperone Involved in the Biogenesis of the CO Dehydrogenase [CuSMoO2] Cluster
relevance: Shows that copper insertion into the binuclear [CuSMoO2] active site of Form I CoxL requires the dedicated chaperone CoxD, explaining why Form II operons lacking coxDEF cannot assemble canonical CODH active sites.
title: The CoxD Protein of Oligotropha carboxidovorans Is a Predicted AAA+ ATPase Chaperone Involved in the Biogenesis of the CO Dehydrogenase [CuSMoO2] Cluster

cr_title: Molecular andCulture-Based Analyses of Aerobic Carbon Monoxide OxidizerDiversity†
relevance: Established the foundational phylogenetic division between canonical CO oxidizers (Group OMP / Form I, AYXCSFR) and putative homologs (Group BMS / Form II, AYRGAGR).
title: Molecular and culture-based analyses of aerobic carbon monoxide oxidizer diversity

cr_title: Catalysis at a dinuclear [CuSMo(O)OH] cluster in a CO dehydrogenase resolved at 1.1-Å resolution
cr_journal: Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences
relevance: Resolves the structural mechanism showing the conserved cysteine of the Form I AYXCSFR motif coordinates the active-site copper atom, explaining why glycine substitution in Form II (AYRGAGR) disrupts binuclear [Cu-S-Mo] geometry.
title: Catalytic mechanism and assembly of the molybdenum and copper containing carbon monoxide dehydrogenase from Oligotropha carboxidovorans

cr_title: Carbon Monoxide Dehydrogenase Activity in Bradyrhizobium japonicum
relevance: Reports purified CODH activity and chemolithoautotrophic growth on CO in Bradyrhizobium japonicum despite possessing only Form II coxL (AYRGAGR), presenting a key empirical exception to Form I exclusivity.
title: Carbon Monoxide Dehydrogenase Activity in Bradyrhizobium japonicum
